meta.name: RV32IM
meta.description: A RISC-V RV32IM processor: one instruction per rising clock edge, its fetches and data accesses go over its SoC bus; the IRQ pins reach it through a PLIC on the same bus

bus.label: Bus
bus.title: The SoC bus the processor uses for its instructions and data; its PLIC answers on it too

resetVector.label: Reset vector (hex)
resetVector.title: Address of the first instruction after a reset when no program has been loaded (a loaded program starts at its entry point)

irqWidth.label: IRQ inputs
irqWidth.title: Number of interrupt inputs (0 to 32); IRQi is source i+1 of the PLIC

plicBase.label: PLIC base address (hex)
plicBase.title: Where the interrupt controller's registers answer on the bus (4 MB, word access only); rounded down to a word

stateVisible.label: Show state
stateVisible.title: Off draws only a grey box on the body, which is faster while the processor runs

program.label: Program
program.title: Run controls, loading a program (ELF file or assembler) and the loaded program with breakpoints

status.label: Status
status.title: Run state, program counter and why the processor stopped

status.notConnected: Not connected to a bus: choose one in the Bus attribute

editor.startTitle: Let the processor execute one instruction per clock edge
editor.stepTitle: Execute one instruction now, without a clock edge
editor.resetTitle: Reset the processor: pc to the program's entry point (or the reset vector), registers unknown, halted
editor.elfTitle: Load an RV32 ELF executable into the bus's memories and reset to its entry point
editor.asmTitle: Write an RV32IM program, assemble it and load it
editor.listingTitle: The loaded program with the current pc; click a line to set a breakpoint

load.done: Loaded {{bytes}} byte(s), entry point {{entry}}; press Start to run

asm.title: Assembler: {{name}}
asm.template:
# RV32IM program. It is assembled and written over the CPU's bus,
# so a SoC Memory must answer at these addresses.
        .text
        .org 0x0
_start:
        li   a0, 0          # sum
        li   a1, 1          # i
        li   a2, 10
loop:
        add  a0, a0, a1
        addi a1, a1, 1
        ble  a1, a2, loop
        ebreak              # stops here: a0 = 55
asm.runTitle: Assemble the program and write it over the bus (Ctrl+Enter)

asm.noCode: The program has no instructions: nothing was loaded
